title: A supplied plant cohort lost 60% of occupied species-plot combinations in the North Cascades in 2018-2020
abstract: We tested whether seed arrival led to persistent seedling occupancy in a North Cascades experiment. We joined a control-adjusted census to 2018 cohort survival counts for 25 supplied plant species. All 241 species-plot combinations with positive initial recruitment had later counts. Only 96 retained the cohort in 2020: 39.8%, with a 95% site bootstrap interval of 32.4-47.3%. Beyond adult cold edges, 11 of 33 combinations retained seedlings. There was no clear extra cold-edge loss under equal species weights. Open sites had 2.18 times the pooled retention of closed sites, but the equal-species contrast was uncertain. The analysis measures a barrier after arrival in one forest experiment. It does not estimate a global climate tracking fraction or a causal canopy effect. Code, source hashes, aggregate results and a retrieval recipe are included.
